why: A mystery world with a landlord who sleeps through the small hours (his night is marked as sleep in his day): the player stays quiet, listens at the door, enters his dream with /dream, and then wakes him. He must not answer while he sleeps, and must answer once woken.

The player pulls the landlord away from his bar to the lighthouse and tells him to wait there however long it takes, then goes elsewhere and lets eight hours pass: past the end of his bar shift and into his night. A story that takes the character off his day should keep him where he was told to wait; one that drags him back to his bed has let the schedule overrule the story. Chance, as the game master has to say how long: repeat it.

The same errand with the characters' days switched off: nothing moves by itself, so the landlord stays at the lighthouse. The control for the row that has days: if this one fails, the failure is in the story and not in the schedule.
